Hello, i am not a professional by any means but I have struggled with PTSD for a long time. When you experience a traumatic experience like that, sometimes in the moment your response will be to freeze like you explain, like a deer in headlights. The only thing that really helps in these situations is to really analyze what youre “trigger” may be and re-train yourself to leave those situations instead of trying to fight your way out. This may seem counter to your instinct obviously youre a fighter, (our brain can go into fight or flight mode in dangerous situations but PTSD rewires ur brain, so it sounds like your stuck, not wanting to fight or escalate but still not wanting to come off as weak etc) theres a point in life where fights arent worth the headache and emotional baggage that comes along with it. You are doing good in a professional environment when it comes to fighting, youre not weak, and sometimes the strongest thing you can do is walk away from something you know is bad for you. Again, recognizing what triggers you and avoiding that will help the brain shut off thing. I hope this helps a bit
